activity_context.topic_title: Linear Combinations of Vectors in N-Dimensional Euclidean Space

examples.knowledge_point: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination
examples.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $\mathbf{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2x & =b \\ 2x & =b-a \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}(b-a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}([\begin{aligned}24 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 2 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $j$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}-j{a}_{2} & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ j[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $j=2.$
